The peer session's rules (on oryn/counseling-intelligence-research, docs 03/07/08/06-family-docs-01-through-09) live in a separate registry, NOT yet merged — see docs/handoffs/research-counseling-intelligence.md for the full topology and the one known direct ID collision (RULE-COUNSEL-056, minted independently by both branches for different rules). rules.statement: Use the Common Data Set's 19-factor academic/nonacademic split as the reference vocabulary for whether a proposed evidence category is admissions-relevant.
Weight academic rigor/grades above any single extracurricular dimension when both compete for a student's limited time.
Never recommend an activity primarily because it 'looks impressive' rather than genuine interest or a genuine profile gap.
Default counseling posture should favor 1-3 sustained, meaningful commitments over many shallow ones.
Treat 'depth over breadth' as directional guidance, not a quantitative formula — never invent a specific 'ideal activity count'.
Do not treat 'no publication' as a research-dimension weakness on its own; mentored process/methodology/independence are legitimate strong evidence without output.
Redundancy/saturation logic must operate per-dimension, not per-activity — one activity legitimately scoring against multiple dimensions is correct, not double-counting.
Treat awards_distinction level-tier point values as unvalidated product heuristics, not research-backed precision.
A counselor should recognize when a student needs more breadth (exploration) rather than more depth, and recommend exploration without treating it as lower-value.
Achievement tier and verification status are independent axes; recommendation confidence should reflect the weaker of the two, never let a high tier claim substitute for low verification.
Do not phrase research-program recommendations as if publication is the expected outcome; frame the mentored process as complete evidence, output as a minority bonus.
Do not phrase competition recommendations as if placing/winning is the expected outcome, even for selective-final-round students.
Do not equate 'finalist'/'semifinalist' language with 'winner' language sharing the same geographic scope word — different tiers, should not score identically.
Evaluate founder/leadership-role attributes on any evidence item regardless of category, not only within nominally leadership/entrepreneurship categories.
Evaluate course rigor relative to what was actually offered to the student, mirroring the School Profile mechanism real admissions offices use.
ORYN's schema has no way to know what curriculum a student's school offers beyond what the student took — treat 'rigor relative to availability' as unresolvable with current data.
Default assumption for a thin activity profile should not be 'low effort' — access/quantity disparities by race and class are real and measurable; initiative within available activities is not.
A gap that cannot be confirmed as access-available should be presented as a hedged observation, never a flat deficiency claim.

Low execution_project_depth evidence for a stated technical interest is a clearer 'real gap' case since self-directed projects have a lower access bar — but must be framed as 'start something small,' never a capability deficit.
Never recommend a specific scarce/competitive pathway (e.g. student government) as THE fix for a leadership gap; recommend the underlying construct instead.
Never recommend 'take more advanced courses' without a hedge acknowledging availability cannot currently be verified.
Read gap severity in light of grade/stage context without altering the computed severity score itself.
Do not assume most students are over-scheduled; large-sample data suggests under-involvement is at least as common.
Do not assert activity intensity causes worse outcomes; at least one longitudinal study found the opposite direction.
Do not cite specific weekly-hour overscheduling thresholds as research-backed; untraceable to a primary source.
Ground 'don't add another activity in an already-strong area' in signal-quality-to-evaluators evidence, not wellbeing claims.
Ground the same recommendation in opportunity cost against the student's actual stated time budget wherever that data exists.
Redundancy strength should depend on tier relationship (escalation/lateral-repeat/level-mismatch/different-sub-skill/cross-dimension-reinforcement), not merely shared ProfileDimension.
Never explain an eligibility/deadline/cost/geography exclusion using redundancy or profile-strength language.
Distinguish 'not valuable' (redundancy/prestige-only) from 'not now' (time-budget/sequencing) in student-facing language.
An avoid_for_now explanation should be fully constructible from already-strong-dimension + tier-relationship + time-budget-opportunity-cost, no wellbeing claims.
Evaluate medicine-track evidence across three areas (clinical exposure, research, community involvement), emphasizing reflection/depth over raw hours.
Reframe undergraduate pre-med evidence guidance for ORYN's actual 14-18 population: shadowing/age-appropriate volunteering, not certified clinical employment.
Never cite MCAT/med-school-admission benchmarks to a high-school-stage student.
Recognize APA's own structured high-school/undergraduate research pathways as a credible official evidence channel for psychology.
Apply the achievement-tier ladder explicitly for psychology-track research: attendance/certificate is a real but lower tier than produced/presented/published output.
Do not extend the 'research requires institutional access' caution uniformly across fields — psychology-track research has a lower access barrier than lab/bench science.
Treat official UN MUN guidance (evidence-based argumentation, real-world grounding) as authoritative for distinguishing genuine engagement from surface participation.
Do not treat MUN achievement alone as sufficient evidence for this family; pair with real-world policy/civic engagement evidence.
Do not read absence of campaign/government/NGO internship evidence as a motivation gap without considering geographic access.
There is no required or specifically-rewarded 'pre-law' major; do not imply one exists.
Recommend broad skill-building across multiple possible majors rather than narrowing a law-interested student's academic path.
Surface court observation as a comparatively low-access-barrier evidence channel for this family, distinct from more consistently access-gated internships.
Treat National History Day as a strong, officially-structured evidence source for the history sub-family, with its own clean achievement-tier progression.
Treat National High School Ethics Bowl as a legitimate, distinct-format (collaborative reasoning, not adversarial debate) evidence source for philosophy/ethics.
For journalism-track evidence, favor a small number of substantive edited/reported pieces over volume; adapt the professional-publication bar down for high-school stage.
Treat Scholastic Art & Writing Awards as a well-established tiered evidence channel; non-medaling submission is still real evidence of sustained craft given the large applicant pool.
Treat architecture/design evidence as portfolio-and-process-centered; process documentation is legitimate evidence on par with finished pieces.
Do not assume a thin design portfolio reflects an access barrier the way a paid program would — core evidence (sketching, self-directed design work) is broadly accessible.
Treat National Portfolio Day's standard guidance as the reference model for visual-art evidence expectations.
Never suggest production value/equipment quality is a priority evidence gap for film/media work; storytelling, composition, and editing are what reviewers name as differentiating.
The tier-aware redundancy model is honestly executable only for the research dimension today (via output_type); treat it as aspirational elsewhere until more evidence-state data exists.
Do not assume US-style curriculum-context admissions mechanisms exist, or don't exist, in non-US systems without verifying per-system.
Before treating a country/curriculum gap as unowned, check whether another concurrent research lane already covers it.
Recognize paid part-time work as legitimate career_exploration/professional-exposure evidence on par with an internship.

[SESSION-LOCAL NUMBERING — COLLIDES WITH PEER's RULE-COUNSEL-056, NOT YET RECONCILED] Exempt career_exploration/intellectual_curiosity candidates from redundancy/saturation discounting for Phase-1 (exploration-stage) students.

Turkish YKS-track admission is exam-score-dominated; extracurricular/development-dimension counseling should not be presented as admissions-strategically important for this pathway the way it would be for US holistic review.
UK UCAS applications reward subject-relevant ('super-curricular') evidence far more heavily than generic extracurricular breadth for competitive courses.

This package's 9-dimension taxonomy and redundancy findings should be treated as general student-development guidance, not assumed to transfer directly as admissions-strategy guidance outside US-style holistic-review systems.
Building a geography/admissions-system-conditional weighting layer above the development taxonomy is the single highest-leverage next research task arising from this package.
France's Parcoursup dossier includes activity/motivation elements weighted by program selectivity; Tier 2 — meaningfully lighter-touch than the US, heavier than Germany/Switzerland.
Germany's admission is Abitur-grade/NC-driven with a large open-admission (zulassungsfrei) category and no general extracurricular-activity factor for the standard domestic pathway.
rules.note: Mechanism upgraded to official-source (DAAD) confidence on a follow-up pass; national prevalence percentage remains genuinely unpublished, not merely unresearched.

rules.statement: Dutch admission is diploma-based/open for most programs; numerus fixus decentralized selection generally does not emphasize extracurricular activities specifically.
rules.note: Mechanism (deadlines, Studiekeuzecheck, selection-step distinction) upgraded to official-source (government.nl/Studielink) confidence; the specific extracurricular-non-emphasis claim remains secondary-sourced.

rules.statement: Italian public-university restricted programs (e.g. IMAT-track medicine) are test-score-driven with no extracurricular factor; private institutions vary and may weight holistically.
Swiss admission is Matura pass/fail-gated for nearly all programs (including ETH/EPFL) with no activity review; medicine's sole exception is a separate aptitude test, not an activity portfolio.
Frame recommendations differently by target-system tier: 'strengthens your application' for Tier 1/2 targets, 'supports your development / matters for a named alternative pathway' for Tier 3 targets.
For a Tier-3-track student, prioritize academic/exam-preparation recommendations as the primary admissions-relevant lever, without implying the other 8 dimensions stop mattering for development.
Key the tier conditional off the student's stated target institution/system, never off nationality, residence, or curriculum alone.

Treat 'rising junior/senior' (roughly grade 11 application, grade 12 program) as a well-evidenced eligibility pattern for flagship structured research programs; a younger student's absence of this evidence type is expected, not a gap.

Evaluate redundancy by whether scope/responsibility escalated across years, not by whether the student stayed in the same organization or switched — same-organization stagnation is the actual redundant pattern, not repetition itself.
Not every pathway's escalation stage requires an external gated program; self-directed curation/narrowing is a legitimate escalation mechanism for portfolio-based creative fields.

For a student discovering an interest late relative to a pathway's typical timeline, recommend a compressed depth-first pathway sized to remaining time; never recommend retroactively demonstrating skipped early-pathway stages.
